articles.title: In defense of feral children
articles.summary: Adults complain and say kids should occupy more space in the world. Then when they do, the world tells them to quiet down. On the Maine island where I live, childhood ends when you’re old enough to catch the 7.15am ferry to school.
body: We live year-round on Peaks Island, a small island accessible only by boat about 3 miles off the coast of Portland. There is an elementary school here, but no middle or high school. So, once island children reach sixth grade, they begin commuting to the mainland by ferry. In many ways, it is a rite of passage.

When my son Theo started middle school, I was thrilled for him – and a little heartbroken. Suddenly, he was across the bay all day, reachable only by boat or cellphone (which he didn’t have). Theo has always belonged to our island as much as he has belonged to me. After years of rinsing sand from his socks and pulling twigs from his hair, sending him away each morning felt a little like prying him loose from his natural habitat.
Fortunately, my son’s daily commute across Casco Bay suggests he has not yet been entirely domesticated.
points: Adults complain and say kids should occupy more space in the world.
Then when they do, the world tells them to quiet down.

articles.title: ‘My reward for waiting in the cold was this painting-like view of the ghat’: Priya Ojha’s best phone picture
articles.summary: There was dense fog over ​a sacred Indian river, but the photographer would not be deterred … When Priya Ojha first arrived at Yamuna Ghat in New Delhi, late in December 2021, she was disappointed.
body: “Visibility was so low that all I could do was wait in the cold,” Ojha recalls. “Around 8am, I heard a voice call out, ‘ Dhoop aa gayi ’ – the sunrays have come out. They were right. This place that had looked like a graveyard slowly became more lively as local priests started their daily routines and boat riders took out their craft for business.”
Ojha recalls that a young boy appeared at her side and said, “Help me make my first ride and I will show you the ghat.” She agreed: “And that’s how I came across this scene.

“The two boats layered between the foreground and the background give a sense of depth, which makes the photo feel more lively,” she adds. “I liked that I captured not just this majestic place and the hundreds of swirling seagulls, but people just like me who had come to experience its beauty, too.”
When she reflects on the photograph now, Ojha is reminded of her patience that morning. “My reward was this painting-like picture of the ghat,” she says. “Just what I had set out for.”

articles.title: Chris Packham: ‘When I was 14, I had a kestrel. I have never been happier or more in love since’
articles.summary: The BBC presenter on listening to techno, wanting his ashes scattered with those of his dogs and shaving with his eyes shut. Born in Southampton, Chris Packham, 65, gained a zoology degree at the University of Southampton.
body: When were you happiest? When I was 14 years old I had a kestrel and I would get up before school to fly it. Nothing else happened that summer. My whole world revolved around that one bird and I have never been happier or more in love since.
What is the trait you most deplore in yourself? My mother used to call me the most tactless boy in the world. Don’t ask me what I think of your new haircut unless you really want the answer.
What is the trait you most deplore in others? Lack of honesty.
What would your superpower be? My mantra is: “Winning is not giving up.” If I’ve got to do something, it doesn’t matter what you throw at me, I won’t give up.

articles.title: The datacentre arms race hits pause in south-east Asia
articles.summary: Power and water constraints are pressuring what seemed like a juggernaut of growth for the region just months ago. In early 2026, Thailand’s datacentre industry was on a roll.
body: As the year has passed, however, what once seemed like a new industrial juggernaut has ground to a halt. Thailand paused construction on 49 projects and approval decisions on 117 more in September 2026, amidst growing concern about the lack of sufficient details for regulation and monitoring. It is not alone in reconsidering datacentre projects. In neighbouring Indonesia, the governor of the country’s most populous province of West Java halted construction on a datacentre due to lack of permits and an incomplete environmental assessment process.

With the global rise of AI usage driving an increased demand for datacentres, south-east Asia has emerged as a surprise centre of growth in the Asia Pacific region. While China has the largest operational datacentre capacity in the region, a 2026 report by real estate firm Cushman and Wakefield shows that south-east Asia has the largest share of under-construction datacentre capacity in Asia Pacific, about 50% of the total. Malaysia and Thailand comprise a large portion of that capacity.

articles.title: Dry Brushing: Why I Do It Every Day And All The Benefits
articles.summary: Dry body brushing has long been touted by celebrities as a wellness ritual to try for enhanced lymphatic drainage and more even skin tone. But does it work? We tested to see.
body: It seems like every time I watch a get-ready-with-me video, the first step of the routine is dry brushing. And while I’ve tried it here and there, I never found myself committing to the act. But this skin-care practice is beloved by not only the likes of Gwyneth Paltrow and Tracee Ellis Ross, but also by functional health doctors and medical professionals as well.

So what is dry brushing? It’s the act of running a bristled brush across your skin while working against gravity (so working toward your torso on limbs) to help with moving the body’s lymphatic system.

Everybody raves about the myriad of health benefits that comes along with dry brushing—from physically exfoliating your skin and eliminating strawberry skin to increasing blood flow and potentially diminishing the appearance of circulation.

articles.title: Black Nails: The Little Black Manicure Is Having a Major Moment
articles.summary: From glossy jet-black to velvet finishes, black nails are this season’s most surprisingly versatile manicure—with fans in Hailey Bieber and Selena Gomez.
body: A slick of jet-black nail polish never goes out of style, and is equal to more than the sum of its parts. It can read grungy, or glam, as a surprisingly versatile shade; and now the inky manicure is enjoying a run as fall’s chicest nail trend. Forget elaborate nail art, milky neutrals, or even the season’s customary burgundy and Bordeaux, because Hailey Bieber, Dua Lipa, Kylie Jenner, and Selena Gomez have all been going back to black.

At the 2026 Academy Museum Gala, Bieber offered a particularly polished take on the trend, pairing her bubblegum-pink Chanel gown with glossy, jet-black nails. Her go-to nail artist, Zola Ganzorigt, used OPI Intelli-Gel in Black Onyx, shaping the nails into elongated almonds and finishing them with a lacquer-like shine. The jewel-black shade was a striking counterpoint to the sweetness of her dress—a glam goth moment—and a marked departure from the glazed, barely-there manicures that have become a Mrs. Hailey Bieber signature.
points: From glossy jet-black to velvet finishes, black nails are this season’s most surprisingly versatile manicure—with fans in Hailey Bieber and Selena Gomez.

articles.title: The 9 Most-Wanted Accessories of Fall—and How to Style Them Now
articles.summary: A silk scarf tied at the waist, a brooch pinned to a blazer, or a strand of pearls tucked beneath a sheer knit are the small styling gestures making the biggest impact.
body: Among all the standout pieces on our fall shopping lists, it was the accessories that emerged as the real heroes. Both the fall and spring collections placed a renewed emphasis on personal style, with accessories offering some of the most compelling ways to make a look your own.

A necklace becomes more personal with the addition of collected charms, while a blazer or knit takes on new character with a brooch pinned to its lapel. Just as important is how these accessories are worn. Consider the strand of pearls layered beneath a sheer knit at The Row, or the silk scarf fastened around the waist like a cummerbund, rather than tied around the neck, at Polo Ralph Lauren. Sometimes, the smallest styling decisions make the biggest impact.

articles.title: 31 Thanksgiving Pies Worth a Second Slice at Breakfast
articles.summary: Bourbon-caramel apple, marshmallow-butterscotch, cranberry meringue, and more reasons to save room for dessert.
body: Some people will happily eat a slice of cheesecake after Thanksgiving dinner. We respect that. But this list of Thanksgiving pie recipes is for those of us who already have our forks poised over the pie table, whipped cream at the ready.

You’ll find the classics: silky pumpkin pie, gooey pecan pie, and apple pie with a double crust and another with cinnamon crumble. Then things get interesting: cranberry meringue with lime-sharpened curd, butterscotch custard with a blanket of toasted marshmallow, a pecan cream pie that doesn’t know when to stop layering. We’ve also got chilled chocolate pies, citrusy custards, and more than a few excellent candidates for breakfast the next morning.

Need more inspiration? Browse our favorite pie recipes or the rest of our Thanksgiving desserts. For help with the pastry, check out our guide to making better pie or the best store-bought pie crusts.

articles.title: The Best Way to Eat Swiss Fondue? Floating on Lake Brienz
articles.summary: Writer Claudia Laroye shares how she and her family bonded over a memorable cheese fondue experience in Interlaken.
body: I could say that I was surprised to find myself and my family floating along in a red Zodiac on the deepest lake in Switzerland, eating cheese fondue and sipping white wine as the sun set. But really, it was all by design. When I designated myself as chief planner for an autumnal family trip to the Alpine nation with my adult children and their partners, I searched for an activity that would knock their socks off. I found it in Interlaken, with a floating fondue experience. Yes, you read that right.

I love Switzerland, and have visited the land where the hills are alive with the sound of cowbells more than 30 times in my life. And while I’ve done many amazing things in and around the Swiss Alps— skiing, hiking, trottinetting, whittling my own Swiss cow from a block of wood—I knew getting my Gen Z crew excited about family time involved finding something a little more unconventional.
